comments.text: It also doesn't matter how old you are.  Stay alert.  I had someone not long ago follow me at the walking trail in the park.  He was in a small pick up and started driving on the grass right next to the walking trail and if I sped up he sped up, if I slowed he slowed.   I am 63 and use a cane, and you wouldn't think this would happen, but this guy was acting very aggressively.  While there had been people there when I arrived, I looked around and everyone had left, realizing this was growing dangerous,  I darted through a door in the chain link fence that leads to a neighborhood and called my husband.  The guy sat in his truck watching me the whole time, just staring me down no expression on his face.  When my husband came, he got out of the our car and started walking toward the truck, then the man sped off and out of the park.  I told my husband he probably should not have done that as the guy might have had a gun, but he was in full husband protection mode bless him, but he listened and admitted he hadn't thought it completely through.  People these days don't play by the same rules and for some one to do this so aggressively, there had to be something wrong with him. Thankfully nothing happened. While this may never happen again, now I feel too afraid to go there alone and it has been one of my favorite safe places to walk for the last 20 years.  I almost left without my phone too that day,  older ones remember to always take your phone if you are out walking.  No matter how old you are if your intuition is telling you something is wrong don't question it.  Don't give people too much benefit of the doubt.  Trust yourself, your intuition and alertness are your greatest weapons.
